title: Etale-origin constructibility for categorical pro-etale coefficients
statement:
Let $X : \mathrm{Scheme}^{u}$ and $\mathcal A : \mathrm{Type}\,u'$ be a concrete Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], with morphisms and underlying sets in universe $u+1$. Use the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site], and derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of $\mathcal A$-valued sheaves. Let $
u^*$ be the canonical comparison inverse image, the left Kan extension along the inclusion of the etale site into the pro-etale site followed by sheafification, and $D(
u^*)$ its termwise induced derived functor. An object $K\in D(\mathrm{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal A))$ satisfies categorical etale-origin bounded constructibility if there exist $L\in D(\mathrm{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal A))$ and an isomorphism $D(
u^*)L\cong K$, where $L$ has bounded cohomology and every cohomology sheaf has a finite partition of $X$ by constructible locally closed immersed subschemes, on each of which its pullback is etale locally constant with finitely generated geometric stalks. Finitely generated here is ConcreteCategory.IsFinitelyGenerated for the specified concrete category; it does not mean finite underlying set for arbitrary coefficients. The finite partition may be different in each cohomological degree. Constructible subsets and locally closed subsets mean [def-weil-constructible-subset] and [def-weil-locally-closed-subset]. This is the source's essential-image definition for arbitrary categorical coefficients, not an identification with intrinsic pro-etale constructibility.
